samples.summary: Two of the three changed `toggleList` call sites (TextEditor and text-box editor) have no test exercising the heading round trip
samples.evidence: The new suite packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts only drives the docs editor (`initialize` from src/view/editor.ts) plus a unit test of `unlistedBlockType`. Grepping `toggleList` across packages shows the only other test touching it is packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:333, which asserts `expect(() => api.toggleList('unordered')).not.toThrow()` — it never checks the resulting block type or headingLevel, so it would pass unchanged whether or not the new exit logic is wired in. TextEditor.toggleList (src/view/text-editor.ts:2166-2170, private, reached via Ctrl+Shift+7/8 in the keydown handler at lines 960/966) has no test at all. The core behavior is covered via the docs editor and the helper, so this is breadth rather than a hole.

samples.summary: The new invariant that `headingLevel` is inert while the block is a `list-item` is asserted nowhere
samples.evidence: The `Block` doc comment added by this change states that "every reader (export, `blockStyleId`, toolbar labels) gates on `type === 'heading'`", which is the only thing keeping a bulleted heading from being styled/exported as a heading. No test locks that in: packages/docs/test/model/named-styles.test.ts:20-47 covers title/subtitle/heading/structural blocks but never a `list-item` carrying `headingLevel` (should be `normal`); packages/docs/test/serialize/markdown.test.ts:78 only exercises real headings; the PDF fixtures (test/export/fixtures/pdf/with-list.json, with-headings-and-links.json) have no block that is both a list item and carries a level; and the frontend `getBlockLabel`/`blockTypeToStyleId` tests do not feed a list-item with a headingLevel. A future regression in any of those gates would silently render bulleted headings as headings with no failing test.
searchedFor: grep headingLevel across packages outside docs/src

samples.summary: Test named "a plain list item returns to a paragraph" passes a paragraph, not a list item
samples.evidence: `expect(unlistedBlockType(makeParagraph('b1', 'body text'))).toEqual({ type: 'paragraph' })` — `makeParagraph` builds `type: 'paragraph'`, so the case described (a list item with no remembered level) is never constructed. The assertion is still meaningful (the helper only branches on `headingLevel`), so this is naming/fidelity rather than fake coverage. The heading counterpart at line 130 does set `block.type = 'list-item'` first.
